newsitem.title: PERU: MRTA warns of reprisals after Peru residence raid.
newsitem.headline: MRTA warns of reprisals after Peru residence raid.

text.p: Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movment (MRTA) reiterated a warning on Friday it would carry out reprisal attacks in response to the military raid at the Japanese ambassador's home that killed 14 of its members.
"Over the next few days there will be actions carried out all across Peru," Norma Velazco, European spokeswoman for the MRTA, said in an interview published on the group's web page Rebel Voice.
Crack Peruvian troops stormed the residence Tuesday in an explosive military assault that secured the release of all but one of the 72 hostages held by the rebels for 126 days.
While acknowledging the bloody end to the standoff was a serious set back for the movement, Velazco warned that it had not been wiped out.
"It is not over yet. We lost the battle, but the struggle continues," she said.
Pesident Alberto Fujimori, who before the Dec. 17 seizure of the ambassador's home had declared the MRTA "dead," has also noted that the group could be preparing for revenge attacks.
But there have been no reports of guerrilla actions since Tuesday.
Velazco accused Fujimori's commandos of torturing MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Carloini and his 13 comrades during the attack.

"Most of the MRTA commando were only killed after the residency had been taken, they were most likely tortured as well. Their dead bodies have not yet been shown to the public," she said, without offering any evidence for the claims.

Commandos killed all 14 of the rebels inside the residence and military sources told Reuters Thursday that two rebels were executed after being captured. Other rebels were killed as they tried to surrender, the sources said.
The body of one rebel leader, Rolly Rojas, was handed over to his family and buried late Thursday, but the whereabouts of the bodies of other MRTA guerrillas, including Cerpa, was a mystery.
